input.quote: (i) Termination by Sanofi for Convenience. Sanofi may terminate this Agreement (A) in its entirety by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed or (B) on a country-by-country or Product-by-Product basis by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed
input.rationale: Section 12.2(a)(i) gives us (Sanofi) an express unilateral termination-for-convenience right, exercisable both in its entirety and on a country-by-country / Product-by-Product basis, which matches the preferred position's requirement of a Customer convenience right. RevMed has no convenience right: its termination rights are all cause-based — material breach (12.2(b)), insolvency (12.2(c)), Sanofi's development of a Competing Product (12.2(d)) and Sanofi's cessation of development activity after notice and a cure period (12.2(e)) — so there is no Vendor walk-away mid-term. No early-termination fee, penalty or accelerated milestone is payable on our convenience termination; the post-termination consequences in 12.3(c) are the customary licence reversion and transition mechanics, and the Termination Product royalties in 12.3(c)(ii)C run in our favour (RevMed pays Sanofi). The specific notice periods in 12.2(a)(i) are redacted ([***]) and should be confirmed as falling in the 30–90 day range, and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts — but a cash refund mechanic is not apt in a collaboration/profit-share structure of this kind, so these are noted rather than flagged. Clause sits at the preferred position; no redline.
